subject: Physics
description: Wave types, frequency, wavelength, speed of sound, Doppler, ultrasonic

questions.stem: Sound waves are best classified as:

options.option_text: Transverse waves like the visible light waves
Longitudinal waves needing a material medium
Electromagnetic waves travelling through vacuum
Standing waves only inside organ pipes only

questions.explanation: Sound = LONGITUDINAL mechanical wave. Particles oscillate parallel to wave direction (compression-rarefaction pattern). Needs a MEDIUM (gas/liquid/solid) — cannot travel in vacuum. Light = TRANSVERSE electromagnetic wave (no medium needed). Distractor 1 confuses sound with light. Distractor 3 — sound is mechanical, not EM. Distractor 4 — standing waves are a special case, not the general nature.

questions.stem: The SPEED OF SOUND in dry air at 20 °C is approximately:

options.option_text: 300,000 km/s, the speed of light
343 m/s, slightly above 1200 km/h
1,500 m/s, the typical speed in water
5,000 m/s, the typical speed in steel

questions.explanation: Sound speed in air: ~343 m/s at 20°C (≈1235 km/h). Increases ~0.6 m/s per °C rise. Faster in DENSER MEDIA — water ~1480 m/s; steel ~5000 m/s; diamond ~12000 m/s. Distractor 1 = speed of LIGHT (≈3 × 10⁸ m/s, vastly faster). Distractor 3 = water. Distractor 4 = steel. The 5-second rule for distance to lightning: 5 sec lag → ~1 km away.

questions.stem: The audible range of HUMAN HEARING is approximately:

options.option_text: 1 Hz to 100 Hz frequency range
20 Hz to 20,000 Hz frequency range
100 kHz to 1 MHz frequency range
1 MHz to 100 MHz frequency range

questions.explanation: Human audible range: ~20 Hz (low rumble) to ~20,000 Hz (high pitch). Decreases with age — older adults often can't hear above 12-15 kHz. INFRASOUND < 20 Hz (elephants, whales communicate; earthquakes). ULTRASOUND > 20 kHz (bats, dolphins use; medical imaging, sonar). Dogs hear up to ~45 kHz; cats ~64 kHz; bats up to 200 kHz.

questions.stem: The DOPPLER EFFECT is the change in observed frequency of a wave when:

options.option_text: The wave passes through different media
Source and observer move relative to each other
Two waves of similar frequency combine
A wave reflects off a hard surface

questions.explanation: Doppler Effect (Christian Doppler, 1842) — apparent change in frequency due to RELATIVE MOTION between source + observer. Approaching → higher pitch (compressed waves). Receding → lower pitch (stretched waves). Examples: ambulance siren rises as it approaches, drops as it passes. Police RADAR guns. Astronomers' RED-SHIFT (galaxies receding) → expanding universe (Hubble). Doppler ULTRASOUND for blood-flow imaging. Distractor 1 = REFRACTION. Distractor 3 = INTERFERENCE / BEATS. Distractor 4 = ECHO.

options.option_text: Water and other dense liquids
Vacuum (no medium for it)
Air at low temperature near zero
Solids like steel or wood

questions.explanation: Sound NEEDS a material medium (solid/liquid/gas). VACUUM has no particles → no compression-rarefaction → no sound transmission. 'In space, no one can hear you scream.' Famous demo: ringing bell in a glass jar; as air is pumped out, sound fades. Distractor 1 — sound DOES travel through water (4× faster than air). Distractor 3 — even cold air conducts sound. Distractor 4 — sound travels FASTEST in solids. Light, in contrast, travels best in vacuum.

questions.stem: ULTRASOUND in medical imaging uses sound waves of frequency typically:

options.option_text: 20 to 20,000 Hz, the audible range only
1 to 20 MHz, well above the audible limit
Below 20 Hz, in the infrasound range
Same as the radio waves used in FM band

questions.explanation: Medical ultrasound: typically 2-15 MHz (general); 1-3 MHz for deeper imaging; 7-15 MHz for superficial. ULTRASOUND = sound above 20 kHz. Used for: fetal ultrasound, abdominal scans, echocardiography, kidney/gallbladder stones, FAST scans (trauma). Non-ionising, safe (unlike X-rays/CT). Doppler ultrasound shows blood flow. Industrial uses: cleaning, welding, distance sensors. Bats + dolphins navigate using ultrasonic echolocation. Distractor 4 — radio waves are EM, different physical phenomenon.

questions.stem: If the WAVELENGTH of a sound wave is 0.5 m and its FREQUENCY is 686 Hz, the speed of sound in that medium is:

options.option_text: 1372 m/s, twice the actual speed
343 m/s, matching speed in air at 20°C
171.5 m/s, half of the actual speed
686 m/s, equal to its frequency only

questions.explanation: Wave speed: v = f × λ = 686 × 0.5 = 343 m/s — matches the speed of sound in dry air at 20°C. Universal wave equation. Distractor 1 = frequency × 2 × wavelength. Distractor 3 = halved (used 0.25 m). Distractor 4 = frequency value alone. Useful: humans speaking ~100-3000 Hz, with wavelengths in air ~3.4 m to 11 cm.
